scope: Staged OTLP JSON serialization and exact uncompressed byte measurement

paired.comparison: Actual pinned Session/Event reporters send to owned local HTTP collectors. Compare their complete decoded request documents and exact UTF-8 byte sizes against Native pure serialization; Native HTTP/queue behavior is not exercised here.

verification.native: 5 passed: wire corpus, timestamp conversion/invalid attribute graphs and direct record-factory regressions.
verification.source: The unchanged OTel package passed 34 tests in C8-GE. This batch additionally captures 44 actual Source channel HTTP cases; no duplicate package run.
verification.scope_reason: Covers wire encoding across both channel record factories, Source SDK attribute admission/count ceilings and resource/scope envelopes.

behavior: OTLP scalar/array/map/byte values retain type tags, with ECMAScript object-key ordering and numeric JSON representation.
Resource null values disappear, while log null attributes encode as empty OTLP values. Ordinary logs drop attributes after 128; Session logs retain unlimited admitted attributes.
Complete canonical event content and Unicode are never truncated by this serializer. Exact bytes include resource/scope envelopes and escaped nested content.
Timestamp conversion preserves nanosecond strings from epoch milliseconds or explicit high-resolution pairs; a caller-supplied origin supports relative-time conversion.
diagnostics: The initial Source-only run intentionally lacked a Native observer and remains labelled a baseline, not parity evidence.
Initial wire comparison found that ResourceImpl discards null attributes before transformation; the separate resource admission now matches.
limitations: This pure serializer is staged; channel queues, byte/count batching, transport headers/retries/cancellation and consumer integration remain subsequent work.
Source paired timestamp observations use absolute business event times; relative-origin and hrtime conversion have Native focused checks, not cross-process clock identity claims.
Implicit SDK tracing context, exception enrichment and arbitrary foreign SDK instrumentation are outside this currently exercised business-record boundary.
No complete migration, Portable/browser or Windows 7 release qualification is claimed.
